title: Memento Mori
text: Happy New Year, everyone. Thank you for your continued support this year as well.
“Gua! Guaaah!”
The freed Filolial-sama bolted off in a panic, still reeling from shock.
“Motoyasu-kun, go calm that one down for me, would you? And could you tell the birds to quit rampaging already? It’s cutting into our share.”
Ark made the request of me. Needless to say, I dashed over to Filolial-sama, who was running about searching for somewhere to flee, and gently wrapped her in an embrace.
“Filolial-sama, please, calm yourself, I beg you.”
“Gua gua!”

Thud, thud! Filolial-sama landed a few kicks on me, but she was clearly panicked—understandable, given how frightened she must have been. If getting kicked by yours truly could soothe her nerves, then I would gladly take as many kicks as she cared to give, I say.
“Settle down. Right now we need to make sure the cat doesn’t decide to attack—otherwise those fools are in for a fate more pitiful than pitiful can describe.”
“Gua!? Gu… gua.”
The moment Hou-kun said that quietly, Filolial-sama gave a start, then prostrated herself, bowing her head low. Ohh… I was truly astonished by Hou-kun’s skill in calming Filolial-sama.
“Waah… that kitten-like look in Motoyasu-kun’s eyes is kind of creepy, or, well, it just kills all the tension, so could you please stop that?”
“You’ve been getting jerked around by every little thing Motoyasu-kun does this whole time. Are you worse with him than you are with those rotten scoundrels?”

“It’s not that I’m ‘bad’ with him, exactly. It’s a feeling hard to put into words. Getting me to play straight man—now that’s a real oddball for you, Motoyasu-kun. So, come on, won’t you? For Motoyasu-kun’s own sake too, please, just leave this to me.”
“I am ever so grateful for absolutely everything, I say!”
Truly, these are worthy god-slayers indeed!
“Sorry, but… that’s a request I can’t grant.”
“Whatever happens, eat this! Die from this one blow! Death-Dam-Dum-Blade Type Ten!”

The one wielding what looked like a gun-shaped sacred weapon pulled the trigger, aiming it at us. What an absurdly lame name for an attack, I say! Truly the mark of a reincarnator. Not a shred of taste to be found.

In response, Ark simply spread her hand, and from it unfurled something massive—resembling the effect Filo-tan produces when using Claw Zero with her Vassal Weapon claws. And she did it without even having a Vassal Weapon.
“Don’t you dare fire off something that weaves in causality for an instant-death effect the weapon itself hasn’t even sanctioned.”
Crack! Ark’s counterattack deflected the bullet, sending it ricocheting away—straight into the crowd of gathered pigs, which then dropped where they stood.
“Bhuya!?”
Plop… the pig that got hit collapsed. It appeared to be dead.
“Wha—you deflected my attack!? That’s not what we were told!”
“Isn’t this thing supposed to be powerless against the likes of us!?”

“Understand that ‘no options’ doesn’t mean the same as ‘nothing to be done.’ Honestly, you lot not realizing that attack itself is a form of cheating is downright hilarious. And who exactly decided it couldn’t be deflected in the first place?”

Ark, her tone growing rougher, answered while shooting them a look of pure contempt. It reminded me of Father, the way he sometimes dodges attacks—not because dodging is forbidden to him, but simply because it isn’t. Father, as Shield Hero, blocks enemy attacks to protect his companions, but when an attack targets only him, he dodges just like anyone else, I say.
“Heh… heheh, seems you’re getting cocky just from killing off a couple of our comrades… but you’re being naive.”
One of the still-unharmed reincarnators began chanting a spell, only to stop midway, his face twisting into shock.
“Wh-why… why won’t the resurrection magic activate!?”
“Looks like you’re chanting some slipshod spell to cobble together a praise-doll. As if I’d allow that. That link to the body’s already been severed—burned away in purgatorial flame.”
“Is this what you people wanted? For me to allow the resurrection of the dead here? Isn’t this exactly what you were trying to show off to me?”
Hou-kun displayed his flame, while Ark raised her left hand, letting several thrashing human souls float up into view.
“Guaaaa…”
Filolial-sama trembled in terror at the sight of Hou-kun and Ark like that. Ah, what magnificent and terrifying figures they were, I say.
“You damn bastards! Tch! Fine, whatever—if we take down you two and capture that cat alive, we can get back everything we lost and more! Let’s go!”
“Right! Everyone! Let’s gooooo!”
“Bhuiiii!”
“Bhu!”
“Give me back my power, you bastaaaaards!”

The reincarnators and pigs called out to their allies, and more and more of their faction gathered around us, preparing to unleash a coordinated assault. Hou-kun raised a hand, and a barrier resembling a firewall sprang up, blocking their advance and their attacks entirely.
“Hey, cat. I’ll say it again—won’t you seriously just leave this one to me? Even if it means I owe you one.”
“Sorry, but that’s not a request I can grant. Seems these fools have no idea just how heavy their sins really are.”
“Haah… how cruel. Though I suppose it’s their own fault for stepping on your landmine.”
Hou-kun said this with a sigh that seemed to come from the very depths of his soul, one of genuine lament.
“Bhu!”
“You lot seem to genuinely believe I’m completely helpless here, but you’d best understand I’ve got other tricks up my sleeve.”

Ark dug her claws hard into her own left arm. Blood burst forth with a spurt, gathering in midair and forming into a floating orb of blood. She flicked the orb away, sending it straight into the mouth of a pig that had been lunging at her.
“Bhu—bhu? Bhu-bhu-bhu-bhuaaaaa!”

The pig gulped down Ark’s blood, and power began surging within it. Was its mana rising? No, that wasn’t it… something far more incredible was happening, or so it felt to me. Could it be… the same effect as that strange medicine I once saw in Filolial-sama’s sanctuary?
“Huh? She just boosted our side’s abilities… that idiot! She went and showed her whole hand!”
“Idiot or not, she seriously has that kind of power!? She’s messing around, but no matter what, we’re taking that thing alive and making them pay for killing our people!”
The reincarnators began laughing at the sight of the empowered pig.
“Bruaaaaa! Bh-bhuyaaaaaaaaaa!?”
Just as the powered-up pig was about to unleash some spell, the moment its eyes fell on Ark, it lurched backward, its face twisting in terror, trembling uncontrollably.
“Bh… bhuya, bhuyaaaaaaaaaa!”
It was wailing and sobbing about something—what on earth was going on?
“What’s wrong with you!? Hey, snap out of it!”
“Bhuya! Bhuyaaaa!?”
The reincarnators shook the pig, but it refused to stop cowering, and to make matters worse, it actually started resisting them.
“Ow!? What are you doing!”
“What the hell are you so scared of!”
“Bhuyaaaaaa!?”
“I don’t know what’s gotten into you, but if you’re gonna thrash around, just die already!”

The reincarnators, treating the pig’s defiance as grounds for punishment, each launched an attack meant to finish it off—but the wounds healed as if time were running in reverse, and the pig kept right on trembling in terror.
“So it really is true that it won’t die, but what in the world is going on here?”
“Want to know?”
Hou-kun said, seeming to mock the reincarnators.
“The hell’s with that attitude, you bastard, don’t go provoking us like you know something we don’t!”
“It really is a sad thing, not knowing. Standing before a cat and being this ignorant… truly foolish.”
“The hell did you say!? Don’t get cocky!”
“Well, perhaps I should just tell you. The cat’s not likely to stop, after all.”
Consider it mercy toward you all. I happen to be in a good mood, Hou-kun said.

“You see… when dealing with a cat, if you’re merely ageless, you’ll only feel a faint sense of bloodlust. But if you go so far as to become truly immortal—unaging and undying both—then a fear check gets triggered. Over and over, eternally, until you fail. She failed that check, and lost her mind.”

I found myself recalling some game based on a certain mythos of fiction, one that had a sanity check mechanic—rolled with dice, and if you failed, your character went insane and became unusable. In other words, standing before Ark while being truly immortal meant you had to keep making that sanity check until you inevitably failed.
“That kind of power—”

“Some fools posing as a certain god tried stacking abilities to escape that judgment, but it was hopeless. You see, all the negativity of the entire world gets pushed onto the cat—so the more omnipotence they stack, the more her power grows in turn. Who was it that called it the anti-existence to the strongest, I wonder? So I really wouldn’t recommend rewriting your abilities and stacking them like that.”
“And that’s that. Now, tremble in fear and die—just this once.”
With a soft whoosh, Ark’s form vanished, and by the time I noticed, the powered-up pig’s head had already been sent flying, its body sliced to ribbons and left rolling on the ground.
『Unto the god who falsely claims immortality, I bestow this gift: an admonition never to be forgotten. Atone for your foolish sin with your very flesh.』
“Memento Mori.”
The attack Ark had unleashed through her spear appeared displayed before us. Memento Mori… I had heard that phrase before. A famous Latin saying, if I recalled correctly.
If memory served… “remember that you must die,” wasn’t it?
So this was that kind of attack, then!? With a delayed spray, fresh blood scattered through the air all around.

The powered-up pig, now nothing but a severed head, let out one final cry of shock. And then, it breathed its last. And yet, somehow, its face seemed to bear an expression of release—as though finally freed from its terror.
“Huh?”
“As if I’d bestow a mercy on my opponent for no reason.”
Ark spat the words out, her eyes burning with rising fury.

“A cat can’t win against even a newborn babe if the conditions aren’t met… but that doesn’t mean there’s no way around it. She’ll force the conditions to align, one way or another. A perfect example of what happens when you take a blessing at face value without thinking it through.”

Hou-kun said this, his eyes filled with pity—not directed at us, but at the reincarnators. Somehow, this reminded me of something. Ah, yes—I recalled some knowledge I’d picked up long ago from a pig, during a discussion about player-versus-player combat in Emerald Online. Since it was against other players, there was a tactic of using enchantments to shift your race classification, turning the tables on opponents wielding weapons specialized against humans. I concluded that whatever power-up Ark had performed on the pig was likely something of that same nature. A laborious method, no doubt—granting the pig her own power, elevating it into something huntable, only to finish it off instantly.
“Understand now? If you know anything about me, you should’ve been able to guess this much. You lot are the real fools here.”
Ark, having gathered even more human souls to herself, spat the words back at the reincarnators with contempt.
“Th-that’s not what we were told!”
